name: list
title: List
summary: Shows a column of related items — a line or more of text with an icon, an avatar or an image — that people read, open one by one, choose from, or put in another order.

anatomy.description: The column that holds the items. It draws nothing and adds no space around them; it carries the semantics of a list or a listbox and moves keyboard focus among the items.
One item's row. It carries hover, focus and press of an interactive item or an option, and the fill of a selected option.

The mark at the start of an item of a list that can be reordered by dragging: the place a pointer or a finger takes hold of the item. It is not a control and is hidden from assistive technology; the move buttons do its work for everyone.
An icon at the start of the row.
An avatar (a round box) or an image (a rounded square) at the start of the row, holding the product's content.
A short line above the headline: a category, a source.
The item's main text and its accessible name.
One or more lines below the headline: a description, a preview.
A short value at the end of the row: a count, a time, a size.
An icon at the end of the row, such as a chevron that says the row opens something.

Two icon-only Buttons in every item of a list that can be reordered, one that moves the item up by one place and one that moves it down. They are the way to reorder that needs no dragging, and are always drawn where the list can be reordered.
A control the product places at the end of a static item (a switch, a checkbox, an icon-only Button). It keeps its own tokens and semantics.

The check at the end of a selected option: the glyph check of the system's icon set, drawn with the icon set's family, fill, weight and optical size. The list draws no mark of its own; a system that wants another check chooses another icon set. Its box is reserved in every option of a selectable list.
A hairline along the bottom of the row, from the start of the text to the row's end.
Gap-then-ring indicator shown for keyboard focus, drawn inside the row.
The list's one live region: empty at rest, it holds the product's sentence that says where an item now stands after it was moved. Not drawn.

props.name: selection
props.description: Whether people choose items: none for a list that shows or opens things, single for choosing one item, multiple for choosing any number. single and multiple make the list a listbox.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the list: what the items are. Required when selection is single or multiple.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the selected option while selection is single; null selects none. The list sets it when an option is chosen and emits change; the product may also set it.

props.name: values
props.description: The values of the selected options while selection is multiple: a list of strings (the platforms take a set). An empty list selects none.

props.name: reorder
props.description: Whether people can put the items in another order. none: the order is fixed. buttons: every item draws a button that moves it up and one that moves it down. drag: the same two buttons, and a handle at the start of every item by which a pointer or a finger drags it to another place. The handle never comes without the buttons: a way to reorder that needs no dragging is always there (LST-36). The list reports the move that was asked for with the move event and never changes the order itself: the items are the product's data. Read only while selection is none, and every item of a reorderable list is static.

props.name: moveUpLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the button that moves an item up by one place: the whole name in the product's language with one place, {headline}, which the list fills with the item's headline ("Move {headline} up", "{headline}を上へ移動"), so that the buttons of two rows are told apart by their names. The product's: Tanrei has no word for it. Empty reads the product's words. Required while reorder is buttons or drag.

places.name: headline
places.description: The headline of the item the button moves.

props.name: moveDownLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the button that moves an item down by one place ("Move {headline} down"). As moveUpLabel.

places.name: headline
places.description: The headline of the item the button moves.

props.name: movedText
props.description: The sentence assistive technology is told once an item stands in its new place, whether it was moved by a button or dropped by a pointer. The product writes the whole sentence in its own language and marks three places in it, which the list fills: {headline} with the moved item's headline, {position} with the place it now has, counted from 1, and {count} with the number of items ("{headline}: {position} of {count}", "{headline}を{count}件中{position}番目に移動しました"). The product's: Tanrei has no sentence for it. Empty reads the product's words. Required while reorder is buttons or drag.

places.name: position
places.description: The place the moved item now has, counted from 1.

places.name: count
places.description: The number of items in the list.

items.name: list-item
items.summary: One row of the list: a headline with optional overline, supporting text, leading icon or media and trailing text, icon or control. It is static, interactive, a link or, in a selectable list, an option.

props.name: headline
props.description: The item's main text, and its accessible name. Required.

props.name: overline
props.description: A short line above the headline.

props.name: supportingText
props.description: Text below the headline. One line of it makes a two-line item; two or more make a three-line item.

props.name: supportingMaxLines
props.description: The lines of supporting text shown before it ends with an ellipsis; 0 shows all of it. The full text still reaches assistive technology.

props.name: trailingText
props.description: A short value at the end of the row.

props.name: leadingIcon
props.description: The name of an icon (a glyph of the system's icon set) at the start of the row.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: The name of an icon at the end of the row.

props.name: leadingMedia
props.description: How the leading slot's content is framed: avatar fits it into a round box, image into a larger rounded square. It replaces leadingIcon.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Makes the item one pressable action that emits its click (a row that changes a setting or opens something in place). Ignored in a selectable list, where every item is an option. Its slots must then hold no interactive element. A row that goes to a page takes href instead and is a link, not a button.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: an address as the platform's links take one (a URL; on the web a path or a fragment as well). Not empty, it makes the item one link — a link item — whether interactive is set or not: the link role, activated by pointer, touch or Enter and not by Space, opened by the platform as its own links are, and drawn exactly as an interactive item is (LST-31, LST-32). Ignored in a selectable list, where every item is an option. Its slots must then hold no interactive element.

props.name: target
props.description: Where the destination opens. same: where the person is — the same tab on the web, the app's own handling of the address elsewhere. new: a new context — a new tab or window on the web, outside the current screen elsewhere — which the item marks with the glyph open_in_new as its trailing icon, unless trailingIcon names one, and says through targetLabel (LST-33). Ignored without href.

props.name: targetLabel
props.description: What assistive technology reads after the link's name while target is new ("opens in a new tab"). Tanrei ships no words of its own, so the product gives them in its own language, as it gives a chip its removeLabel. Required while target is new; ignored otherwise.

props.name: value
props.description: Identifies the option: the list's value (single) or values (multiple) select the option whose value they hold, and change carries it. Unique within the list; needed for an option, unused by a static, interactive or link item.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents activation. The arrow keys still reach it. Ignored for a static item: an item that is not an action, a link or an option has nothing to disable.

props.name: divider
props.description: Draws a hairline along the bottom of the item. The product sets it on every item but the last, or at the end of a group.

slots.name: leading
slots.description: The avatar's or the image's content: an image, or a monogram for an avatar. Drawn only while leadingMedia is avatar or image.

slots.name: trailing
slots.description: A control of the product's own at the end of a static item: a switch, a checkbox, an icon-only Button.

events.name: click
events.description: The interactive item or the link item was activated by pointer, touch, keyboard or assistive technology. A link item emits it before its destination opens; a product that takes the navigation itself (a client-side router) cancels it (LST-32).

events.name: change
events.description: The user changed the selection; carries value (single) or values (multiple) after the change.

events.name: move
events.description: The user asked for an item to stand in another place, by a move button or by dropping it. Carries from, the item's index among the list's items when the move began, and to, the index it is to have once it has moved, both counted from 0 (moving the second item up is from 1, to 0; dropping the first item after the third is from 0, to 2). Emitted once per move, never for a move that ends where it began, and never during a drag. The product reorders its items; the list has changed nothing.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates an enabled interactive item by pointer, touch, Enter or Space — a link item (LST-31) by pointer, touch or Enter — THE list SHALL emit that item's click exactly once.

WHILE an interactive item or an option is disabled THE list SHALL NOT emit its click or change for it and SHALL expose the disabled state to assistive technology; the arrow keys SHALL still reach it, so that people learn it exists, but Space, Enter, pointer and touch SHALL NOT activate it.

WHILE an interactive item or an option is hovered, keyboard-focused or pressed THE list SHALL render its container, headline, overline, supporting text, trailing text, icons, mark and opacity from the component tokens of its condition in the highest-precedence active state, with precedence pressed over focused over hovered; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT select the focused state.
behavior.verify: Test under the `acme` fixture system, which values hovered, focused and pressed differently.

behavior.text: WHEN an item receives keyboard focus THE list SHALL show the focus ring inside the item's container, so that the list's scrolling ancestor cannot clip it, without animation; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT show it.

WHERE an interactive item or an option is shorter than the minimum target THE list SHALL make its container at least sys.target.touch tall for touch input and sys.target.pointer tall for fine pointers, because rows that touch cannot extend a hit area over each other; a platform that cannot tell the input type SHALL use sys.target.touch. The whole row, leading media and trailing elements included, SHALL be the item's hit area.

WHILE an interactive item or an option is disabled THE list SHALL render its container, headline, overline, supporting text, trailing text, icons, mark and opacity from the disabled component tokens of its condition, and SHALL apply that opacity to the whole item, its leading media included.
WHEN selection, reorder or leadingMedia names a value the list does not define THE list SHALL render with the default value, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

WHEN the list item is pressed by pointer, touch, Enter or Space THE list item SHALL show the pressed state without delay and SHALL keep it visible for at least sys.motion.duration.press-hold, even when the press ends sooner.

WHILE pressed THE list item SHALL answer as sys.behavior.pressed-feedback names: overlay applies the pressed tokens to the whole container at once; ripple grows the pressed state layer from the point of contact (from the center for keyboard activation); dim applies the pressed opacity to the whole control and draws no state layer; none draws no answer to the press. Under ripple and dim only the container color stays with the state under the press; headline, overline, supporting text, trailing text, icons, mark, opacity and shape still come from the pressed tokens. Under none every part stays with the state under the press. The ripple grows over comp.list.motion.feedback-duration with comp.list.motion.state-easing, fades over comp.list.motion.state-duration with comp.list.motion.state-easing once the press has ended and press-hold has passed, and appears whole where motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Test under a system that sets each value; `m3-like` is ripple, `cupertino` is dim, the default is overlay.

behavior.text: THE list item SHALL ease its container corners by sys.shape.corner-smoothing (0 is a quarter circle, 0.6 the iOS continuous corner; a platform with only the OS curve draws it for any amount above 0) and show its keyboard focus as sys.behavior.focus-style names (ring or glow); a platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value and state that in its README.
behavior.verify: `cupertino` is continuous; the `acme` fixture system is glow. The default rows are square, so the smoothing shows only under a system that rounds them.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is none, an item's interactive is false and its href is empty THE list SHALL render the item from the resting tokens of the unselected condition, SHALL NOT make the item focusable or emit its click, SHALL draw no hover, focus or press answer on it, SHALL ignore its disabled, and SHALL leave a control in its trailing slot its own tokens, semantics and focus stop.

WHILE selection is none THE list SHALL expose the list role, each item as a list item with its position and the list's size, and an interactive item as one element with the button role, or a link item (LST-31) as one element with the link role, inside its list item; WHILE selection is single or multiple THE list SHALL expose the listbox role named by label (multi-selectable while selection is multiple) and each item as an option with its selected state, its position and the list's size, and SHALL ignore interactive and href.

WHEN the user activates an enabled option of a list whose selection is single and whose value is not that option's value THE list SHALL set value to the option's value, so that the option that was selected becomes unselected, and emit change once; WHEN the option is already selected THE list SHALL change nothing and SHALL NOT emit change, because a single choice is never cleared by its own option.
WHEN the user activates an enabled option of a list whose selection is multiple THE list SHALL add the option's value to values, or remove it when values holds it, and emit change once.

WHILE the list holds an interactive item or an option THE list SHALL be one Tab stop — the item that had focus last, or else the first selected option, or else the first enabled item — and SHALL move focus to the next and previous item with Down Arrow and Up Arrow without wrapping, to the first and last with Home and End, and to the next item whose headline begins with the typed characters when printable characters are typed within one second of each other; moving focus SHALL NOT change the selection, and Space or Enter SHALL activate the focused item, Enter alone a link item (LST-32). Static items SHALL NOT take focus.

THE list SHALL lay out an item as one row: comp.list.container.padding-inline-start from the start edge, the handle of a list that is reordered by dragging (LST-44), the leading icon or leading media, then the text column (overline, headline and supporting text, stacked) taking the remaining width, then the trailing text, the trailing icon, the two move buttons of a reorderable list (LST-37), the trailing control and, in a selectable list, the mark, each comp.list.container.gap from the next, and comp.list.container.padding-inline-end from the end edge; WHEN the layout direction is right-to-left THE list SHALL mirror the row, and a ripple SHALL still grow from the point of contact.
behavior.verify: Fixtures: each renders one list 360 wide holding the fixture's items in order; the fixture's props apply to the list and each item's props to that item. With leadingMedia avatar the leading slot holds the first letter of the item's headline; with image it is empty and shows comp.list.media.container.color. Hover, focus and press are unit-tested through the resolved tokens, not snapshot.

behavior.text: THE list SHALL make an item at least comp.list.container.height.one-line tall with a headline alone, comp.list.container.height.two-line tall with one more line of text (an overline, or supporting text on one line) and comp.list.container.height.three-line tall with two or more, SHALL pad its content by comp.list.container.padding-block above and below, and SHALL grow with its content and with enlarged text beyond that, never clipping it; it SHALL center the leading and trailing elements on the text column in a one- or two-line item and align them with the top of the text column in a taller one.

THE list SHALL draw the headline in comp.list.headline.typescale, the overline in comp.list.overline.typescale, the supporting text in comp.list.supporting-text.typescale and the trailing text in comp.list.trailing-text.typescale; the headline, overline and trailing text SHALL wrap rather than truncate; WHILE supportingMaxLines is greater than 0 the supporting text SHALL end with an ellipsis after that many lines, and its full text SHALL still reach assistive technology.

THE list SHALL draw leadingIcon at comp.list.leading-icon.size and trailingIcon at comp.list.trailing-icon.size through the icon helper, with the family and fill of the item's condition (selected for a selected option, otherwise unselected), sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max; an empty name SHALL draw nothing and leave no space.

WHILE leadingMedia is avatar THE list SHALL fit the leading slot's content into a box of side comp.list.avatar.size clipped to comp.list.avatar.shape, and WHILE it is image into a box of side comp.list.image.size clipped to comp.list.image.shape, each filled with comp.list.media.container.color behind the content and handing it comp.list.media.content.color as its foreground; WHILE it is none THE list SHALL NOT draw the leading slot, and WHILE it is avatar or image it SHALL NOT draw leadingIcon. A monogram in the avatar is set in comp.list.headline.typescale, centred.

WHILE selection is single or multiple THE list SHALL reserve a box of side comp.list.mark.size at the end of every option and, while the option is selected, draw the glyph check of the system's icon set centered in it, in the mark color of the option's condition, with sys.icon.family.selected, sys.icon.fill.selected, sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max, and SHALL NOT mirror it when the layout direction is right-to-left; THE list SHALL draw no mark of its own (no path, shape or character of its own for the check). WHEN an option becomes selected or unselected THE list SHALL fade the check in or out without moving or scaling it, and change the option's colors, over comp.list.motion.state-duration with comp.list.motion.state-easing, and SHALL make the change at once where motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Under the `acme` fixture system, whose icon set is static (a family per selection state), the check is drawn in its selected family; in the default system the glyph's box is comp.list.mark.size, the same as comp.list.trailing-icon.size, and the fixtures single-selected, multiple-selected and selected-disabled show it.

behavior.text: WHILE divider is true THE list SHALL draw a line of comp.list.divider.thickness in comp.list.divider.color along the bottom edge of the item, inside its height, from the start of the text column to the row's end edge; the line SHALL keep its color, and its full opacity, in every state and condition of the item (a disabled item's opacity does not reach it) and SHALL be hidden from assistive technology.

THE list SHALL name an interactive item or an option by its headline and describe it by its overline, supporting text and trailing text, in reading order; icons, the mark, the divider and the leading media SHALL be hidden from assistive technology unless the product names the media; WHILE headline is empty THE list SHALL still render the item and in debug builds report that it has no accessible name, and WHILE selection is single or multiple and label is empty it SHALL report that the listbox has no accessible name.

WHILE an item is interactive or an option THE item's slots SHALL contain no interactive element; a platform that can inspect its slot content (the web, on every slot change) SHALL report one in debug builds, and a platform that cannot SHALL state the rule in its README and docs page.

WHEN the colors of an interactive item or an option change between states THE list SHALL animate them over comp.list.motion.state-duration with comp.list.motion.state-easing, and SHALL change them at once where motion is reduced.

THE list SHALL render an option as selected, from the selected condition, WHILE selection is single and value equals the option's value, or selection is multiple and values holds it, and every other option from the unselected condition; WHEN value or values names no option THE list SHALL select nothing for that name, and WHEN an option's value is empty or repeats another option's THE list SHALL still render it; in debug builds it SHALL report each of these.

IF the icon set cannot draw the check yet (its font is still loading or failed to load) THE list SHALL draw nothing in the check's place, never the glyph's name as text, SHALL keep the box of side comp.list.mark.size, SHALL still expose the option's selected state, and SHALL show the check once the icon set can draw it, without the fade of LST-21.

THE list SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the list is shown THE list SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its selection, its scroll position and its focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render. On the web the test is owed with the other right-to-left tests.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE list SHALL draw an item's leading icon and trailing icon mirrored left to right exactly when the system's icon set marks that glyph's name as mirrored or the product forces mirroring for that use, and unmirrored when the product forbids it: the icon helper mirrors the glyph inside its own box, about the box's vertical centre line, changing neither its place, size, color and fill nor the order LST-16 gives. THE list SHALL NOT mirror a glyph itself, and SHALL NOT mirror content the product gives as an image or a view of its own rather than by a glyph's name. A leading avatar or image and the check of a selected option (LST-21) are never mirrored.
behavior.verify: arrow_forward, chevron_right, reply and send are marked by the default icon set; check, close, search and play_arrow are not. Test one marked and one unmarked name in right-to-left, the marked one again with mirroring forbidden and the unmarked one with it forced, and the marked one in left-to-right (never mirrored there).

behavior.text: THE list SHALL lay out an item's overline, headline, supporting text and trailing text as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: each takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right word, a number with its sign or unit, a telephone number and an address keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE list SHALL still place each and align its lines by the layout direction, not by the text's own, and SHALL cut supporting text limited by supportingMaxLines that does not fit (LST-18) at the end of its own direction, so that a left-to-right label in a right-to-left layout loses its right end and never its beginning.

WHILE selection is none and an item's href is not empty THE list SHALL make the item a link item, whether its interactive is true or false: one element with the link role and not the button role inside its list item, named and described as LST-23 says, its slots held to LST-24; the platform's own link to href (the web's anchor element; SwiftUI's Link; on Compose, Flutter and React Native an element with the platform's link semantics whose address is opened by the platform's opener), so that whatever the platform gives a link — on the web its context menu, opening in a new tab or window, copying and dragging its address, and the address shown before it is followed — is the platform's, and not the list's to draw or to take over; and everything this spec says of an interactive item other than its role and its keys — its states, focus ring, minimum height, press answer, corners, motion, disabled look and its place in the list's one Tab stop and arrow-key order (LST-2 to LST-6, LST-8 to LST-10, LST-15, LST-25) — SHALL hold for a link item from the same tokens, with no look of its own for a link and none for a destination already visited.
behavior.verify: Fixture links: its first two items are drawn exactly as interactive items with the same content. On the web the item's shadow root holds an anchor with the href; assert the role link inside a list item, and that the arrow keys move between link items.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates a link item by pointer, touch or Enter THE list SHALL emit that item's click exactly once and then open href where target names, unless the product cancelled that click, in which case it SHALL open nothing: the product's own router has taken the navigation. It SHALL show the pressed state as LST-8 and LST-9 say and SHALL NOT hold the navigation back for sys.motion.duration.press-hold. THE list SHALL NOT activate a link item on Space, which on the web scrolls the page as it does on any link, and SHALL NOT show the pressed state for it; WHERE the platform gives its links other keys or gestures (on the web a modified or a middle click that opens a new tab, on Apple platforms a long press that previews) THE list SHALL leave them to the platform.
behavior.verify: On the web: Enter on the focused link item follows the link and fires its click once; Space fires no click and leaves the page to scroll; a click listener that calls preventDefault() keeps the page where it is.

behavior.text: WHILE an item is a link item and its target is new THE list SHALL open href in a new context — on the web a new tab or window that is given no handle to the page that opened it; on the other platforms outside the screen the person is on, as the platform's opener decides — and, WHILE the item's trailingIcon is empty, SHALL draw the glyph open_in_new of the system's icon set as the item's trailing icon, as LST-16 places and LST-19 draws trailingIcon: at comp.list.trailing-icon.size, in the trailing-icon color of the item's condition and state (comp.list.unselected.trailing-icon.color at rest, and so on), through the icon helper, which mirrors it in a right-to-left layout because the icon set marks its name (LST-29), and hidden from assistive technology. WHILE trailingIcon names a glyph THE list SHALL draw that glyph and no mark of its own: the product has chosen what that place shows. Whether a mark is drawn or not THE list SHALL expose targetLabel as the end of the item's description, after what LST-23 gives it, and WHILE targetLabel is empty SHALL still render and in debug builds report that a link that opens a new context does not say so. WHILE target is same THE list SHALL draw no mark and SHALL ignore targetLabel.
behavior.verify: Fixture links: the third item shows the mark at the row's end, 24 large under the default system; fixture links-rtl shows it at the left, mirrored.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is none and an item's href is not empty and its disabled is true THE list SHALL NOT make the item a link that can be followed: it SHALL render the item as LST-6 says, the mark of LST-33 with it, SHALL expose the link role with the disabled state and no destination, SHALL keep it reachable by the arrow keys as LST-2 keeps any disabled item, SHALL NOT emit its click, and SHALL open nothing by any means the platform gives a link (on the web the anchor carries no href, so there is no context menu entry, no drag and no new tab for it).
behavior.verify: Fixture links: the fourth item. On the web its anchor has no href attribute, role link and aria-disabled true; Down Arrow still reaches it and Enter does nothing.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is single or multiple THE list SHALL ignore every item's href, target and targetLabel, as it ignores interactive (LST-12), and in debug builds SHALL report an option that has an href: an option holds a state and is not a destination. WHEN an item's target names a value the list does not define THE list SHALL treat it as same, and in debug builds report the unknown value. IF an item's href is only white space, or names a script to run rather than a place to go (the web's javascript: scheme), or cannot be read as an address by the platform, THE list SHALL make the item what its interactive makes it, without a destination, and in the last two cases report it in debug builds.

WHILE selection is none and reorder is buttons or drag THE list SHALL be reorderable: it SHALL draw the two move buttons in every item (LST-37) and, WHILE reorder is drag, the handle as well (LST-44), and SHALL NOT draw the handle without the buttons under any value, so that every way of using the list has a way to move an item that needs no dragging. THE list SHALL render every item of a reorderable list as a static item (LST-11), ignoring its interactive and its href, and in debug builds SHALL report an item that has either: a row that is itself one button or one link cannot hold the buttons that move it (LST-24). WHILE selection is single or multiple THE list SHALL ignore reorder, draw no move button and no handle, and in debug builds report it: an option cannot hold a button. THE list SHALL never change the order of its items itself: it SHALL report the move that was asked for (LST-39, LST-47) and draw the items in the order the product gives them.
behavior.verify: Fixtures reorder-buttons and reorder-drag. Unit: a list with selection single and reorder buttons draws no move button and reports once; an item with interactive or href in a reorderable list has no element with the button or the link role for its row. After a move button is pressed and the product changes nothing, the items are in the order they were.

behavior.text: WHILE the list is reorderable THE list SHALL draw in every item, after the trailing icon and before the trailing control, two buttons: first, in reading order, the one that moves the item up, showing the glyph arrow_upward of the system's icon set, then the one that moves it down, showing the glyph arrow_downward; each an icon-only Tanrei Button of the text variant at Button's medium size and default width, drawn from Button's own tokens, the two comp.list.move-buttons.gap apart, measured so that each keeps at least sys.target.touch along the row (two buttons narrower than that stand apart by what is missing), both centred on the text column as LST-17 places a trailing element. Each SHALL be a Button in its press, its target, its states and its focus ring (BTN-5, BTN-8, BTN-9, BTN-10), and a focus stop of its own in reading order, before the item's trailing control: the list handles no key for them and is not one Tab stop (LST-15 speaks of interactive items and options, and a reorderable list has neither). THE list SHALL NOT mirror the two glyphs in a right-to-left layout, where up is still up, and SHALL keep their order: the button that moves up comes first in reading order, so at the right of the other.
behavior.verify: Fixtures reorder-buttons and reorder-buttons-rtl. Unit: Tab from before the list reaches the first item's enabled move button, then the next, then that item's trailing control; no arrow key moves focus.

behavior.text: THE list SHALL name the button that moves an item up by moveUpLabel and the one that moves it down by moveDownLabel, each with its place {headline} filled by the headline of its item, so that two buttons of two rows are told apart by their names; neither SHALL carry the headline a second time as a description. IF the word given has no place {headline} THE list SHALL name the button with it as it is written and in debug builds report that every row's button has the same name; another text between braces, and a brace that opens or closes nothing, SHALL be kept as written and reported. THE list SHALL have no words of its own: it SHALL take moveUpLabel, moveDownLabel and movedText from its own prop and, WHILE that is empty, from the product's words of the same name, and from nowhere else. IF neither gives moveUpLabel or moveDownLabel WHILE the list is reorderable THE list SHALL still draw that button and keep it working, SHALL expose it without a name, and in debug builds SHALL report the missing words once per word and page or screen, naming the prop. IF neither gives movedText THE list SHALL announce nothing after a move (LST-42) and SHALL report it the same way.
behavior.verify: Unit: with the words given once through the product's words and no prop, every move button is named; each button's name holds its item's headline in the sentence's place; with a prop, the prop wins; with neither, the buttons are drawn, work, have no accessible name, and the missing keys are moveUpLabel, moveDownLabel and movedText.

behavior.text: WHEN the user activates the button that moves up of the item at index i, counted from 0, THE list SHALL emit move exactly once with from i and to i − 1, and WHEN the user activates the button that moves down it SHALL emit move exactly once with from i and to i + 1; one activation is one whole move, with nothing to confirm and nothing to cancel. THE list SHALL NOT move the item itself and SHALL NOT emit an item's click for it.
behavior.verify: Unit: in reorder-buttons, pressing the second item's move-up emits one move with from 1 and to 0; Enter and Space on the focused button do the same; no click is emitted by the item.

behavior.text: WHILE the list is reorderable THE list SHALL disable the button that moves up of its first item and the button that moves down of its last item, and both buttons of an item that is alone, as Button disables (not focusable, the disabled state exposed), and SHALL still draw them, so that every row has the same parts in the same places and a button does not arrive under a pointer after a move.
behavior.verify: Fixtures reorder-buttons (the first and the last item) and reorder-single-item.

behavior.text: WHEN the product, after a move the list emitted, gives its items in an order in which the moved item stands at the index to, THE list SHALL draw that order (LST-43), SHALL set every item's position anew for assistive technology (LST-12), SHALL announce the move (LST-42), and SHALL keep keyboard focus with the moved item: WHILE focus was on one of its move buttons when the move was asked for, on that same button of the item now at to, or on its other move button where that one has become disabled (LST-40), whether the product moved the item it had or gave a new one for the same content; WHILE focus was elsewhere THE list SHALL NOT move it. The same button keeping focus is what lets a person move an item several places by pressing one key several times. IF the product has not given such an order by the time comp.list.motion.reorder-duration has passed since the move was emitted THE list SHALL take the move as refused: it SHALL announce nothing, leave focus where it is and draw the items as the product has them.
behavior.verify: Unit: pressing Enter three times on the fourth item's move-up, with a product that reorders in its handler, leaves that item first, focus on its move-down button (move-up is disabled there) and three announcements, the last with position 1. The same with a product that replaces every item element. With a product that ignores the event, focus and order are unchanged and nothing is announced.

behavior.text: WHILE the list is reorderable THE list SHALL hold one live region of its own, polite, empty at rest and not drawn, and SHALL have nothing else of the list announce a move. WHEN a move has taken effect (LST-41) THE list SHALL put into it movedText with its three places filled — {headline} by the moved item's headline, {position} by the place the item now has, counted from 1, and {count} by the number of items in the list, the two numbers written as the platform writes a whole number in the language of the list — so that it is announced once, after what is being read; a later move SHALL replace what the region holds and SHALL NOT queue behind it. THE list SHALL fill the places as a word with places is filled: each place wherever and however often the product wrote it; any other text between braces, and a brace that opens or closes nothing, left as it is written and in debug builds reported once per page or screen, naming the prop; a brace written twice drawn as one brace; and the headline inserted as plain text of its own direction, isolated from the sentence (LST-30). THE list SHALL announce nothing when an item is lifted and nothing while it is dragged over other items (LST-45, LST-46): the handle is a pointer's, the person using it is watching the item, and assistive technology is told the one thing that happened, where the item now stands.
behavior.verify: Unit, with movedText "{headline}: {position} of {count}": moving Sent from third to second of three sets the live region to "Sent: 2 of 3"; a second move replaces the text; a drag over two rows writes nothing until the drop has taken effect. With movedText "{headline} {place}" the text keeps "{place}" and one report is made. With movedText "{{headline}} {position}" the text is "{headline} 2" and nothing is reported.

behavior.text: WHEN the order of the items of a reorderable list changes THE list SHALL move every item whose place changed from where it was drawn to its new place over comp.list.motion.reorder-duration with comp.list.motion.reorder-easing, along the list's axis and without fading or scaling it, the focus ring travelling with the item that holds focus; an item that is new or gone SHALL appear or leave at once. WHERE motion is reduced THE list SHALL draw the new order at once.
behavior.verify: Unit: after a move button, the two items that changed places are drawn between their places for the length of the motion and at rest after it; with reduced motion the first frame after the change is the final one.

behavior.text: WHILE the list is reorderable and reorder is drag THE list SHALL draw in every item, at the row's start before the leading icon or the leading media, the glyph drag_indicator of the system's icon set in a box of side comp.list.handle.size, in comp.list.handle.color, through the icon helper with sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max, centred on the text column as LST-17 places a leading element, and never mirrored. Its hit area SHALL be at least sys.target.touch square for touch input and sys.target.pointer square for fine pointers, reaching over the row's start padding and the gap beside it without changing the layout and without reaching over another control. THE handle SHALL be hidden from assistive technology and SHALL NOT be a focus stop: it is not a button, a press on it that ends without a drag SHALL do nothing and draw no answer, and the move buttons do its work for a keyboard, a switch, a voice and a screen reader. WHERE the pointer is a fine one THE list SHALL show over the handle the platform's cursor for something that can be held (grab). THE list SHALL draw the handle of an item that is alone in its list as well, and SHALL take no drag from it.
behavior.verify: Fixtures reorder-drag and reorder-drag-rtl. On the web: the handle is aria-hidden, has no tabindex and no role; a click on it emits nothing.

behavior.text: WHEN the user presses a handle with touch, a pen or the primary button of a mouse and moves past the platform's touch slop (8 points where the platform names none, for every kind of pointer) THE list SHALL lift that item: at once, with no long press, because the handle is there to be dragged and holds nothing else a press could mean. From then until the drag ends THE list SHALL draw the item above the other items of the list, as wide as its row and with its content unchanged, filled with comp.list.dragged.container.color and with the shadow comp.list.dragged.container.elevation, the fill and the shadow arriving over comp.list.motion.state-duration with comp.list.motion.state-easing, and SHALL leave a gap of the item's height where it would stand if it were dropped now. A touch that begins on a handle SHALL NOT scroll the page or the list's scrolling ancestor; a touch or a press that begins anywhere else on a row SHALL scroll, select text and do whatever it did before, and SHALL never lift an item: THE list SHALL take no drag from a long press on a row, which is the platform's to answer (a menu, a selection, a preview). A press of another mouse button, and a second pointer while one item is carried, SHALL lift nothing.
behavior.verify: Unit: a touch pressed on the second item's handle and moved 12 down draws that item with the dragged fill and shadow and a gap where it stood, without any wait; a press held 800 ms on the headline and then moved lifts nothing and the page scrolls. The row at rest has no fill.

behavior.text: WHILE an item is dragged THE list SHALL move it with the pointer along the list's axis only, by the distance the pointer has travelled since the press, in the frame the pointer moves and without a motion of its own, never further than the first item's and the last item's place, wherever the pointer goes, outside the list included. WHEN the centre of the dragged item passes the centre of a neighbouring item THE list SHALL move that neighbour by the dragged item's height to the other side of the gap, over comp.list.motion.reorder-duration with comp.list.motion.reorder-easing, so that the gap is always where the item would be dropped. WHILE the pointer is nearer than sys.target.touch to the top or the bottom edge of the list's nearest scrolling ancestor and the list reaches beyond that edge THE list SHALL scroll that ancestor toward it, the faster the nearer, and keep the gap under the dragged item. WHILE the drag lasts THE list SHALL draw no item and no button hovered or pressed, SHALL let nothing it draws be selected as text or be taken by the platform's own drag and drop, SHALL show a fine pointer the platform's cursor for something held (grabbing), and SHALL emit nothing.
behavior.verify: Unit: in reorder-drag, the first item dragged down by one and a half row heights draws the second item in the first place and the gap in the second; dragged sideways by 200 it does not leave its column; dragged below the last item it stays in the last place. No move is emitted before the release.

behavior.text: WHEN the user releases a dragged item THE list SHALL move it into the gap over comp.list.motion.reorder-duration with comp.list.motion.reorder-easing and take the dragged fill and shadow from it over comp.list.motion.state-duration. IF the gap is not where the item stood when it was lifted THE list SHALL emit move exactly once, with from the index the item had and to the index of the gap, both counted from 0, and SHALL keep drawing the items as they were dropped until the product gives that order or comp.list.motion.reorder-duration has passed since the event, whichever comes first, so that a product that reorders in answer to the event shows no frame of the old order; it SHALL then draw the product's order, announce the move and keep focus as LST-41 says (focus inside the moved item stays with it; focus elsewhere is not moved), and where the product gave no such order the items SHALL go back to their places over the same motion. IF the gap is where the item stood THE list SHALL emit nothing and announce nothing.
behavior.verify: Unit: the first of three items dropped after the third emits one move with from 0 and to 2; with a product that reorders in its handler no frame shows the old order; with a product that ignores the event the item is back in the first place after the motion. A drag released where it began emits nothing.

behavior.text: WHILE an item is dragged, WHEN the user presses Escape, or the platform cancels the pointer or takes it for a gesture of its own, or the window or the app loses focus, or the product changes the list's items, its reorder or its selection, THE list SHALL end the drag without a move: it SHALL return the item and its neighbours to the places they had over comp.list.motion.reorder-duration with comp.list.motion.reorder-easing, SHALL emit nothing, SHALL announce nothing and SHALL leave the scroll position where the drag brought it. Escape SHALL be taken by the list while a drag lasts and SHALL NOT reach an overlay that holds the list, so that putting an item back does not also close the dialog it is in.
behavior.verify: Unit: the first item dragged past the second and Escape pressed is the first item again, no move was emitted and a dialog around the list is still open.

behavior.text: WHERE motion is reduced THE list SHALL still move a dragged item with the pointer, which is the person's own movement and not a motion of the list's, SHALL give it the dragged fill and shadow at once, SHALL put a neighbour on the other side of the gap at once (LST-46), SHALL put a released item into the gap or back to its place at once (LST-47, LST-48), and SHALL scroll its ancestor near an edge as LST-46 says.
behavior.verify: Unit, with reduced motion: every frame of a drag shows each neighbour in one of its two places and never between them.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE list SHALL draw the handle in the platform's text color, SHALL draw a dragged item on the platform's background color with an edge sys.border.hairline wide in the platform's highlight color all around it, in place of a fill and a shadow that are not drawn there, and SHALL leave the move buttons to be drawn as Buttons are there, a disabled one in the platform's disabled text color.
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: the dragged item has an outline in Highlight and covers the rows under it.

behavior.text: WHERE the handle, the move buttons and the trailing control of a reorderable list would leave the text column less than half the width of the row — a narrow screen, enlarged text — THE list SHALL place the move buttons and the trailing control on a line of their own below the text column, at the row's end and in the same order, comp.list.container.padding-block below the text, and SHALL do so for every item of the list at once, so that the buttons of all rows stand under each other. The row SHALL grow with it (LST-17) and the handle SHALL stay at the row's start, centred on the first line of the text column. At 200% text size in a list 320 wide no text SHALL be cut or lie under a control, no control SHALL be smaller than its target, and nothing SHALL need scrolling sideways.
behavior.verify: Fixture reorder-drag-long-text at a stage 320 wide and at 200% text size: the buttons are below the text in every row and the headline wraps.

behavior.text: WHILE the list is reorderable THE list SHALL leave a control in an item's trailing slot its own tokens, semantics and focus stop (LST-11), after the move buttons in reading and focus order: a button that removes the item is the product's, and so is the removal. WHEN the product takes away an item that holds keyboard focus THE list SHALL move focus to the control in the same place — the same move button, or the control of the trailing slot — of the item that now stands where that item stood, else of the item before it, and where that control is absent or disabled to the first control of that item that can take focus; WHEN the last item is taken away THE list SHALL leave focus to the product, which knows where a person adds an item. THE list SHALL announce nothing for a removal or an addition: what was removed is the product's to say.
behavior.verify: Unit: with a remove button in every trailing slot, removing the second of three items while its remove button has focus puts focus on the remove button of the item that was third; removing the last item puts it on the remove button of the one before.

accessibility.role: list (listbox while selection is single or multiple)

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the list (to the item focused last, the first selected option or the first enabled item) and out of it. A list of static items is not a tab stop; focus moves through the controls in its items.
Moves focus to the next or previous item, without wrapping. Does not change the selection.
Moves focus to the first or last item.
Moves focus to the next item whose headline begins with the characters typed.

Activates the focused item: an interactive item emits its click; an option is selected (single) or switched (multiple). A link item is activated by Enter alone: Space does what it does on any link (on the web it scrolls the page).

Moves focus through the controls of each item in reading order: the button that moves it up, the button that moves it down, then the control of its trailing slot. A disabled move button is passed. The handle is not a stop.

Moves the item one place up or down. Focus stays on the same button of the moved item, so pressing again moves it again; where the item has reached the first or the last place, focus goes to its other move button.

keyboard.keys: Escape (while an item is dragged by a pointer)
keyboard.action: Puts the dragged item back where it was. Nothing is moved.

accessibility.labeling: An item's headline is its accessible name; its overline, supporting text and trailing text are its description. A selectable list is a listbox named by label. Icons, the mark and dividers are decorative. While target is new, a link item's targetLabel ends its description. The content of an interactive item, a link item or an option is presentational: it is read as part of the item, not as separate elements. In a reorderable list each move button is a button named by moveUpLabel or moveDownLabel and described by its item's headline; the handle is hidden. After a move the list's one live region says movedText, with the item's headline, its new position and the number of items.
notes: One item kind, list-item, and four kinds of row chosen by props: static (selection none, interactive false, no href) shows content and may hold the product's own control in its trailing slot; interactive is one button inside its list item; a link item (href) is one link inside its list item; an option (selection single or multiple) is chosen. A list may mix static, interactive and link items; a selectable list holds only options.
Selection is the list's: value names the selected option of a single-select list, values those of a multiple-select list, each by the options' value.

A row whose whole width toggles a setting is a static item with a switch in its trailing slot, the switch named by the headline (label = headline, labelHidden). The row does not forward presses to the switch: the switch's own hit area is the control, as the one-control-per-focus-stop rule requires.
The list does not scroll or virtualize: the product places it in its own scroll view, or builds it lazily with the platform's lazy list and states the set size where the platform needs it.
Text size does not clip an item: rows grow at 200% text size and the headline wraps.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

An item with a destination is a link (a control with a destination is a link): the link role, the platform's own link, Enter and not Space, so that on the web a row of an index or of a table of contents can be opened in a new tab and its address copied. No visited state is drawn. A list of links is still a list, moved through with the arrow keys as one tab stop; a site's navigation with a current page is the navigation drawer's, not a list's.
A link item that opens a new context shows the open_in_new mark as its trailing icon and says so through targetLabel; the words are the product's.

A list is reorderable in two forms, and the first is complete by itself. buttons: two buttons in every item, which serve a keyboard, a pointer, touch, a switch, voice control and a screen reader alike and meet the requirement that anything done by dragging can be done with single presses. drag: the same buttons and a handle for a pointer or a finger. There is no keyboard mode on the handle (lift, move with the arrows, drop): it would serve the keyboard alone, would need its keys taught in words, and would keep a held item as a state that focus can leave.

The order is the product's data. The list emits move with from and to and draws the items in the order the product then gives; a product that refuses a move changes nothing and the list announces nothing.

A reorderable list holds static items only: a row that is one button, one link or an option cannot hold the move buttons (the one-control-per-focus-stop rule). A list whose rows open something and can also be reordered is left to a later revision; it needs a keyboard model in two directions.

What a reorderable item may hold besides its text and media: one control of the product's in its trailing slot, as any static item, typically a button that removes the item. The list keeps focus in the list when the item with focus is removed (LST-52).

movedText is one of the product's words with places to fill. The product writes the sentence, so the order of the words is its language's; the list fills in a name and two numbers and builds no phrase of its own.

The list is a column. Dragging is along its axis only, so a right-to-left layout changes where the handle and the buttons stand in the row and nothing about the direction of a move. A row of things that can be reordered (chips, tabs, cards) is not a list and is not covered here.

web.name: tanrei-list

list-item.name: tanrei-list-item
list-item.notes: A child element of `tanrei-list`, with kebab-case attributes (`supporting-text`, `supporting-max-lines`, `trailing-text`, `leading-icon`, `trailing-icon`, `leading-media`) and `leading` and `trailing` named slots. Its host has the role listitem or option; an interactive item draws a shadow element with role button and tabindex, as the interactive card does, and fires `click`. With `href` the item's shadow root holds an `<a>` in place of the element with role button, inside the host's list item. The link form: `href` is the item's `href` attribute; `target` is the `target` attribute with the values `same` and `new` (the HTML spellings `_self` and `_blank` are read as those two; anything else is `same` and reported); `targetLabel` is the `target-label` attribute. Web-only, forwarded to the anchor and to nothing else: `rel` (to which `new` adds `noopener`) and `download`. Cancelling `click` (`preventDefault()`) cancels the navigation, which is how a client-side router takes it; a modified or a middle click is the browser's. A disabled link is the anchor without `href`, with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`, as the navigation drawer's destination already is. Space is not handed to the press controller. `element.click()` follows the link.

web.notes: `tanrei-list` (selection, label, value, values) holds `tanrei-list-item` children. It sets its own `value` or `values` (an array property; the `values` attribute is not reflected) before firing `change`, as a native control does. Focus moves among items by a roving tabindex. Each item is a separate element, so the list sets `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` on them. Reordering: `reorder` is the `reorder` attribute; `moveUpLabel`, `moveDownLabel` and `movedText` are the attributes `move-up-label`, `move-down-label` and `moved-text`, and keys of `setWords()`. `move` is a `CustomEvent` whose `detail` is `{ from, to }`; it bubbles, is not cancelable, and the list moves no element: the product reorders the `tanrei-list-item` children (or its framework does), and the list sees it as a change of its children. The move buttons are two `tanrei-button` elements in each item's shadow root, `aria-describedby` the headline; the handle is an `aria-hidden` element with `touch-action: none` and pointer capture for the length of a drag, and the dragged item and its neighbours are moved by transforms, so the product's elements never change place under it. The live region is one visually hidden `role="status"` element in the list's shadow root. Focus after a move is set on the item now at `to`, because a child that is moved in the document loses focus and a framework may give a new element. Before the element is defined (no script) the items are plain children in the order written and nothing can be moved.

swiftui.name: TanreiList

list-item.name: TanreiListItem
list-item.notes: `TanreiListItem(_ headline:, overline:, supportingText:, …)` in the list's view builder, tagged with `.tag(value)`. The initializer with `action:` makes it interactive, as `Button`. `leading:` and `trailing:` are view builders; `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`. Not built on this platform yet: the `TanreiListItem` initializer that takes `destination: URL` in place of `action:` draws the same control as a SwiftUI `Link`, so the address is opened by the environment's `openURL` — an app that routes addresses itself provides an `OpenURLAction`, which is how the navigation is cancelled — and VoiceOver reads the link trait. `target: TanreiLinkTarget = .same` and `targetLabel` (the accessibility hint) are parameters of that initializer alone.

swiftui.notes: SwiftUI's `List(selection:)` idiom, drawn by Tanrei: `TanreiList(selection: Binding<V?>)` is single, `Binding<Set<V>>` is multiple, and the initializer without a binding is none, so the binding's type is selection and its content is value or values. An option is selected when the binding holds its tag, and writing the binding is change. `label` sets the list's `accessibilityLabel`. The rows are not `List` rows: `List`'s own row chrome and separators cannot be tokenised. Ships the previous revision of the check today (the check stroked as a path at comp.list.mark.width in a 20 box, drawn along its path when an option is selected); other parts of this spec are not built on this platform yet. Not built on this platform yet: `TanreiList(reorder: .buttons, onMove: { from, to in … })`, with the three words as parameters or from the environment's words. `onMove` receives the two indices of the spec, not SwiftUI's `IndexSet` and insertion offset; the README shows the one line that turns them into `Array.move(fromOffsets:toOffset:)`. The move buttons are also exposed as the accessibility custom actions of the row; the announcement is posted as an accessibility announcement.

compose.name: TanreiList

list-item.name: TanreiListItem
list-item.notes: `TanreiListItem(headline, value = …, …)` called in the `TanreiList { }` content lambda. A non-null `onClick` makes it interactive; `enabled` is the inverse flag. `leadingContent` and `trailingContent` lambdas are the slots. Not built on this platform yet: a `TanreiListItem` with `href: String` (`onClick` is then optional and called first) opens the address through `LocalUriHandler.current` after `onClick`; an app that routes addresses itself provides its own `UriHandler`. Compose has no link role for a clickable element (only link annotations inside text), so the node drops `Role.Button` and carries no role, and the README says so. `target: TanreiLinkTarget = TanreiLinkTarget.Same`; `targetLabel` is appended to the node's state description.

compose.notes: `TanreiList(selectionMode, contentDescription, selectedValue | selectedValues, onSelectionChange) { TanreiListItem(…) }`, a column with `selectableGroup()` semantics; for long data the same items go into a `LazyColumn` inside `TanreiList`. State hoisting: the caller keeps `selectedValue` (single) or `selectedValues: Set<String>` (multiple) and moves it from `onSelectionChange`, which receives the new selection. Ships the previous revision of the check today (the check stroked as a path at comp.list.mark.width in a 20 box, drawn along its path when an option is selected); other parts of this spec are not built on this platform yet. Not built on this platform yet: `reorder: TanreiListReorder = TanreiListReorder.None` and `onMove: (from: Int, to: Int) -> Unit`; the caller moves the element of its hoisted list. The move buttons are also given as `customActions` of the row's semantics; the announcement is a polite live region node. Items need stable keys for the motion of LST-43.

flutter.name: TanreiList

list-item.name: TanreiListTile
list-item.notes: `TanreiListTile<T>(value:, title:, subtitle:, …)` widgets in the list's `children:`, with `ListTile`'s names. A non-null `onTap` makes a tile interactive; `enabled: false` disables it. `leading` and `trailing` are widgets. Not built on this platform yet: a `TanreiListTile` with `href` (a `Uri`; `onTap` is then optional and called first) has `Semantics(link: true)` with the address as its `linkUrl`. The package has no plugin dependency, so the address is opened by the nearest `TanreiLinkOpener`, an inherited widget the app provides once (calling `url_launcher`, or its own router); without one the control opens nothing and reports it in debug builds. `target` is a `TanreiLinkTarget`; `targetSemanticLabel` is the semantics hint.

flutter.notes: `TanreiList<T>(selectionMode:, selected: Set<T>, onSelectionChanged:, semanticLabel:, children: [TanreiListTile<T>(…)])`, as `SegmentedButton`: one `Set<T>` holds the selection, with at most one member while selectionMode is single, so `selected` is both value and values. The caller moves it from `onSelectionChanged`. Ships the previous revision of the check today (the check stroked as a path at comp.list.mark.width in a 20 box, drawn along its path when an option is selected); other parts of this spec are not built on this platform yet. Not built on this platform yet: `reorder: TanreiListReorder.none` and `onMove: (int from, int to)`. `to` is the index the item has after the move, not the insertion index of the framework's reorderable list, which is one more for a move downward: the README says so. The announcement goes through `SemanticsService.announce`. Tiles need keys.

react-native.name: List

list-item.name: ListItem
list-item.notes: The element type of the list's `items` array: `{ headline, overline?, supportingText?, …, value?, disabled?, divider?, onPress?, leading?, trailing? }`, where `leading` and `trailing` are elements. A non-null `onPress` makes an item interactive. Not built on this platform yet: an item with `href` has `accessibilityRole="link"` and opens the address with `Linking.openURL` after `onPress`, unless `onPress` called `event.preventDefault()`. `target` is `"same" | "new"`; `targetLabel` is the `accessibilityHint`.

react-native.notes: `<List items={ListItem[]} selectionMode value | values onSelectionChange accessibilityLabel>`; controlled, the caller moves `value` or `values` from `onSelectionChange`. The list does not scroll or virtualize (see the accessibility notes); for long data the product builds its own `FlatList` and states the set size. The roles are set with React Native's `role` prop and each option's selected state with `accessibilityState.selected`; what the native screen reader announces for a listbox is the platform's. The arrow keys work where a hardware keyboard is attached. Ships the previous revision of the check today (the check stroked as a path at comp.list.mark.width in a 20 box, drawn along its path when an option is selected); other parts of this spec are not built on this platform yet. Not built on this platform yet: `reorder="buttons"` and `onMove={({ from, to }) => …}`; the caller sets its state. The move buttons are also `accessibilityActions` of the row; the announcement goes through `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility`. Dragging needs a gesture responder on the handle alone.
